title: Eggs in mustard sauce with broccoli
desc: Soft-boiled eggs in a light mustard sauce with broccoli. A cheap, quick classic.
reheat: Warm the sauce gently; add the eggs at the end.
left: Cold eggs and sauce next day for lunch.
trouble: Whisk hard or pass it through a sieve.

steps.t: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
steps.w: Cooling stops the yolk going grey.
steps.c: Yolk just set, slightly soft in the middle.
steps.m: Cracking cold eggs into fast-boiling water splits them; lower them in gently.
steps.img: peeled boiled eggs on a board

steps.t: Steam or simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed broccoli

steps.t: Make the sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock a little at a time. Simmer 3 minutes until it coats a spoon.
steps.w: Cooking the flour removes the raw taste.
steps.m: Adding all the stock at once makes lumps.
steps.img: a pale sauce being whisked in a saucepan

steps.t: Take off the heat, stir in the cream, mustard and nutmeg. Season, add the halved eggs and warm through.
steps.w: Mustard loses its bite if it boils.
steps.m: Boiling after the mustard goes in.
steps.img: halved eggs in a pale mustard sauce with broccoli

title: Chicken fricassee with carrots and a few peas
desc: Chicken in a light lemon cream sauce, without the rice.
trouble: Poach it gently; a hard boil tightens it.
goes: Carrots and peas are in the pan.

steps.t: Simmer the chicken and carrots in the stock, covered, for 10 minutes. Lift them out and keep the stock.
steps.w: Poaching keeps the chicken soft and makes the base for the sauce.
steps.m: A rolling boil makes it tough.
steps.img: chicken pieces and carrots in stock

steps.t: Make the sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock a ladle at a time. Simmer 4 minutes until it coats a spoon.
steps.w: This turns the poaching stock into the sauce.
steps.m: Rushing the stock in makes lumps.
steps.img: a pale sauce simmering

steps.t: Add the cream, chicken, carrots and peas. Heat 3 minutes, then add lemon juice and parsley and season.
steps.w: Lemon goes in last so it stays fresh.
steps.m: Too much lemon: start with half.
steps.img: chicken fricassee in a pan with carrots and peas

title: Creamy chicken strips with broccoli
desc: Thin chicken strips in a paprika and onion cream sauce.
reheat: Simmer gently with a splash of water.
trouble: Pan not hot enough or too full; fry in two batches.

steps.t: Fry the chicken strips in the oil on high heat for 4 minutes until browned, then lift out.
steps.w: Brown bits in the pan flavour the sauce.
steps.m: Crowding the pan makes it steam.
steps.img: chicken strips browning in a pan

steps.t: Steam or simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed broccoli

steps.t: Fry the onion for 3 minutes, add the paprika for 20 seconds, then the stock, scraping the pan.
steps.w: Paprika burns fast; stock stops it.
steps.m: Burnt paprika tastes bitter.
steps.img: onions and paprika deglazed with stock

steps.t: Make the sauce: stir in the cream and mustard, return the chicken and let it bubble gently 3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Season.
steps.w: A short simmer keeps the chicken soft.
steps.m: Long boiling dries it out.
steps.img: creamy chicken strips with broccoli

title: Salmon in mustard sauce with carrots
desc: Frozen salmon portions, pan-fried, with a quick mustard and dill sauce.
reheat: Eat fresh; salmon dries out when reheated.
trouble: Leave it until it releases by itself.
Take off the heat and whisk in a spoon of water.
ing: frozen portions, defrosted in the fridge overnight

steps.t: Steam or simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed carrots

steps.t: Pat the salmon dry, salt it, and fry in the oil on medium-high, 4 minutes skin side then 2 minutes on the other. Lift out.
steps.w: Dry fish browns instead of steaming.
steps.c: Pink colour has climbed most of the way up.
steps.m: Moving it too early tears the skin.
steps.img: salmon frying skin side down

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour the stock and cream into the salmon pan, scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 2 minutes until it coats the back of the spoon. Off the heat, stir in the mustard and dill and season.
steps.w: Mustard stays sharp if it does not boil.
steps.m: Boiling it after the mustard.
steps.img: salmon with mustard dill sauce and carrots

title: Salmon with lemon butter and broccoli
desc: The quickest fish night: salmon, broccoli, butter and lemon.
trouble: Lower the heat; add it at the end.
Take it off when just pink in the middle.
ing: frozen portions, defrosted in the fridge overnight

steps.t: Steam or simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed broccoli

steps.t: Pat the salmon dry, salt it, and fry 4 minutes skin side and 2 on the other. Lift out.
steps.w: Dry fish browns.
steps.m: Moving it too early tears the skin.
steps.img: crisp salmon in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: lower the heat, melt the butter in the salmon pan, add the lemon juice and 1 tbsp water and swirl the pan for 30 seconds until it looks creamy, not oily. Stir in the parsley and spoon the sauce over the salmon.
steps.w: Low heat stops the butter burning.
steps.m: High heat burns it in seconds.
steps.img: salmon with lemon butter and broccoli

title: Pan-fried meat patties with carrots
desc: Pan-fried meat patties from minced beef. Counts as red meat.
reheat: Oven or pan until piping hot.
trouble: Chill 10 minutes, or add a spoon of breadcrumbs.
Do not press them in the pan.

steps.t: Mix the mince, half the onion raw, the egg, breadcrumbs, mustard, parsley, salt and pepper. Shape 6 flat patties.
steps.w: The onion keeps them moist.
steps.c: Holds together without sticking to your hands.
steps.m: Overworking makes them dense.
steps.img: raw meat patties on a board

steps.t: Steam or simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed carrots

steps.t: Fry the patties in the oil on medium heat for 5–6 minutes a side.
steps.w: Medium heat cooks the middle before the outside burns.
steps.m: Pressing them squeezes out the juice.
steps.img: browned meat patties with carrots

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the patties out and pour away all but 1 tsp of the fat. Pour 100 ml water into the pan, scrape the brown bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon and stir in 1 tsp of the mustard. Let it bubble 2 to 3 minutes on medium-high until it has shrunk by half, add pepper and pour the sauce over the patties and carrots.
steps.w: The brown crust the patties leave is meat flavour, and water plus mustard makes it a gravy.
steps.c: It is brown, a bit glossy and thinly coats the back of the spoon.
steps.m: Keeping all the fat in, so the sauce is greasy.

title: Mince skillet with peppers and carrots
desc: A one-pan mince dish, with no noodles needed. Counts as red meat.
trouble: Higher heat; let it sit before stirring.

steps.t: Brown the mince in the oil on high for 6 minutes without stirring too much.
steps.w: Browning is where the flavour comes from.
steps.m: From frozen, break it up as it thaws and wait for the water to cook off.
steps.img: mince browning in a pan

steps.t: Add onion, garlic, carrot and pepper and fry 5 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute.
steps.w: Frying the paste removes its raw taste.
steps.m: Burning the paprika: add the stock quickly.
steps.img: peppers and mince with paprika

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour in the stock, scrape the dark paste off the bottom with a wooden spoon and simmer 6 minutes until it is thick and coats the mince. Season.
steps.w: A short simmer brings it together.
steps.m: Too much stock makes it soup.
steps.img: a pan of mince with peppers and carrots

title: Scrambled eggs with broccoli
desc: Soft scrambled eggs with broccoli for the veg.
trouble: Take off the heat while still slightly wet.

steps.t: Steam or simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes grey and watery.
steps.img: a bowl of steamed broccoli

steps.t: Beat the eggs with salt. Melt the butter on low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly for 3 minutes.
steps.w: Low heat gives soft curds.
steps.m: High heat makes them dry.
steps.img: soft scrambled eggs with broccoli

title: Buttered mixed vegetables with chicken
desc: Carrots, broccoli, cauliflower and a few peas in a little butter, with pan-fried chicken.
reheat: Pan with a splash of water.
trouble: Drain well before the butter goes in.
Take it off after 5 minutes a side.

steps.t: Simmer the carrots 3 minutes, add broccoli and cauliflower for 4 more, then the peas for the last minute. Drain.
steps.w: Each veg goes in by how long it needs.
steps.m: Adding everything at once overcooks the broccoli.
steps.img: carrots, broccoli, cauliflower and peas in a colander

steps.t: Salt the chicken and fry in the oil, 5 minutes a side. Rest 2 minutes.
steps.w: Resting keeps it juicy.
steps.m: Moving it too often stops it browning.
steps.img: chicken fillets in a pan

steps.t: Toss the veg in the butter and parsley, season, and serve with the sliced chicken.
steps.w: Butter carries the flavour.
steps.m: Too much heat browns the butter.
steps.img: buttered mixed vegetables with sliced chicken

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour 4 tbsp water into the chicken pan, scrape the brown bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 1 minute on medium heat. Take the pan off the heat and swirl in 1 tsp of the butter until it melts. Spoon the sauce over the sliced chicken.
steps.w: The brown bits from the chicken plus butter make a small glossy sauce so the chicken is not dry.
steps.c: It looks glossy and slightly thick, not greasy.
steps.m: Adding the butter on high heat so it just turns to oil.

title: Chicken schnitzel with broccoli and lemon
desc: Thin chicken schnitzel with a light crumb, lemon and broccoli.
reheat: Oven or air fryer to crisp up.
trouble: Pat dry and press the crumbs on firmly.
goes: Broccoli; the lemon-butter sauce goes over both.

steps.t: Simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked broccoli

steps.t: Salt the flattened chicken. Dip in beaten egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
steps.w: Thin chicken cooks before the crumb burns.
steps.m: A thick crumb adds carbs and oil.
steps.img: crumbed chicken on a board

steps.t: Fry in the oil on medium heat, 3–4 minutes a side. Lift the schnitzel onto a plate and keep the pan with its brown crumbs.
steps.w: Medium heat browns the crumb evenly.
steps.m: Crowding the pan makes it soggy.
steps.img: golden chicken schnitzel with broccoli and lemon

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour off the excess oil but keep the brown crumbs. On low heat, melt the butter until it foams and smells nutty. Squeeze in the lemon, add 2 tbsp water, scrape the brown bits off the pan with a fork and swirl for 1 minute. Pour over the schnitzel and the broccoli.
steps.w: The brown crumbs, butter and lemon make a sharp, rich sauce in one minute.
steps.c: Looks creamy and coats the spoon.
steps.m: High heat burns the butter black.
steps.img: lemon butter sauce foaming in a frying pan with brown crumbs, a fork scraping the pan, half a lemon beside it, home kitchen

title: Paprika chicken with cauliflower
desc: Chicken in a red pepper and tomato sauce, no cream.

steps.t: Simmer the cauliflower in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked cauliflower

steps.t: Brown the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes and lift out. Fry onion, garlic and peppers for 5 minutes.
steps.w: Brown bits flavour the sauce.
steps.m: A crowded pan steams the chicken.
steps.img: chicken and peppers in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: stir in the paprika for 20 seconds, add the tomatoes, scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon and return the chicken. Simmer 9 minutes until the sauce is thick. Season.
steps.w: Paprika needs fat, but burns fast.
steps.m: Burnt paprika tastes bitter.
steps.img: paprika chicken with cauliflower

title: Lemon chicken with buttered carrots
desc: Simple pan chicken with a lemon and stock glaze.
reheat: Pan with a splash of stock.

steps.t: Simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked carrots

steps.t: Salt the chicken and fry in the oil, 5 minutes a side. Rest on a plate.
steps.w: Resting keeps the juices in.
steps.m: Cutting it straight away loses the juice.
steps.img: chicken fillets browned in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour the stock and lemon juice into the chicken pan, scrape the brown bits off the bottom and boil 3 minutes until reduced by half. Off the heat, swirl in the butter and parsley until glossy and spoon the sauce over.
steps.w: Reducing concentrates the flavour.
steps.m: Boiling after the butter splits the sauce.
steps.img: lemon chicken with buttered carrots

title: Curry chicken strips with broccoli
desc: Curry-ketchup flavour with chicken strips and a sugar-free curry tomato sauce.

steps.t: Simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked broccoli

steps.t: Fry the chicken in the oil on high for 4 minutes and lift out. Soften the onion for 3 minutes.
steps.w: Browned chicken holds up in the sauce.
steps.m: Crowding the pan.
steps.img: chicken strips in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: stir in the tomato paste, curry powder and paprika for 1 minute, pour in the stock and scrape the brown bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon. Return the chicken and simmer 3 minutes until the sauce coats the chicken. Season.
steps.w: Frying the spices brings out the flavour.
steps.m: Burnt spices taste bitter.
steps.img: curried chicken strips with broccoli

title: Meatballs in tomato sauce with broccoli
desc: Meatballs in tomato sauce, with no pasta — a good use for frozen mince. Counts as red meat.

steps.t: Mix the mince, half the onion, the egg, breadcrumbs and salt. Roll 10 balls.
steps.w: Egg and crumbs bind them.
steps.m: Too wet: add a spoon of crumbs.
steps.img: raw meatballs on a board

steps.t: Brown them in the oil for 5 minutes and lift out. Soften the rest of the onion and the garlic for 3 minutes.
steps.w: Brown crust adds flavour.
steps.m: Turning too early tears them.
steps.img: meatballs browning in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: add the tomatoes and oregano, scrape the brown bits off the bottom, return the balls and simmer 10 minutes, turning them, until the sauce is thick and coats them. Cook the broccoli alongside and spoon the sauce over it.
steps.w: A short simmer finishes the meatballs.
steps.c: Thick red sauce, the balls are coated.
steps.m: A hard boil breaks them.
steps.img: meatballs in tomato sauce with broccoli

title: Tuna patties with carrots
desc: Patties from tinned tuna. Counts as a fish meal.
trouble: Drain the tuna very well and chill 10 minutes.

steps.t: Simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked carrots

steps.t: Mix the drained tuna, egg, breadcrumbs, spring onion, mustard, lemon and parsley. Shape 6 patties.
steps.w: Dry tuna holds together.
steps.m: Wet tuna falls apart.
steps.img: tuna patties on a board

steps.t: Fry in the oil on medium heat, 3 minutes a side.
steps.w: Turn once only.
steps.m: Flipping early breaks them.
steps.img: golden tuna patties with carrots

steps.t: Make the sauce: in a small bowl, stir the rest of the mustard with the rest of the lemon juice, 1 tbsp water and a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth. Put a spoon of the sauce next to each patty and over the carrots.
steps.w: Fish patties are dry, and a sharp mustard-lemon sauce wakes them up without new ingredients.
steps.c: It is smooth and runs slowly off the spoon.
steps.m: Using it neat without water, so it is too strong.

title: Farmer's omelette with peppers and onion
desc: Farmer's omelette, without the potatoes.
trouble: Non-stick pan and a little more butter.
Take it off while the top is slightly wet.

steps.t: Fry the onion and pepper in the butter for 5 minutes.
steps.w: Softened veg stops the omelette going watery.
steps.m: Burning the butter: lower the heat.
steps.img: peppers and onion softening

steps.t: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour in, and cook on low for 4 minutes with a lid.
steps.w: The lid sets the top without flipping.
steps.m: High heat makes it rubbery.
steps.img: a farmer's omelette with peppers

title: Beef patty steak with a fried egg and broccoli
desc: Mince steak, a fried egg on top, broccoli on the side. Counts as red meat.

steps.t: Mix the mince with half the onion, salt, pepper and mustard. Shape 2 flat steaks.
steps.w: Flat steaks cook evenly.
steps.m: Overworking makes them tough.
steps.img: two raw mince steaks on a board

steps.t: Simmer the broccoli in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked broccoli

steps.t: Fry the steaks in the oil on medium heat, 5 minutes a side. Lift out and fry the eggs in the same pan.
steps.w: Medium heat cooks the middle.
steps.m: Pressing the steaks squeezes out the juice.
steps.img: mince steak topped with a fried egg and broccoli

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the eggs out. Pour 4 tbsp water into the pan, scrape the brown bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon and stir in 1 tsp of the mustard. Let it bubble 1 minute on medium heat until slightly thick and pour the sauce over the steaks.
steps.w: The steak crust in the pan is flavour, and a splash of water and mustard turns it into a quick gravy.
steps.c: It is light brown and slightly thick, not just water.
steps.m: Wiping the pan between steaks and eggs and losing the brown bits.

title: Beef patty steak with fried onions and carrots
desc: Classic mince steak with browned onions. Counts as red meat.
trouble: Lower the heat and add a splash of water.
Take it off after 5 minutes a side.

steps.t: Mix the mince with half the onion, salt, pepper and mustard. Shape 2 flat steaks.
steps.w: Flat steaks cook evenly.
steps.m: Overworking makes them tough.
steps.img: two raw mince steaks on a board

steps.t: Simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked carrots

steps.t: Fry the steaks in the oil, 5 minutes a side, and lift out. Fry the sliced onions in the same pan for 6 minutes until brown.
steps.w: The pan juices brown the onions.
steps.m: Too high a heat burns them before they soften.
steps.img: mince steak with browned onions and carrots

steps.t: Make the onion sauce: keep the brown onions in the pan, pour in 100 ml water and scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon. Stir in 1 tsp of the mustard, salt and pepper and let it bubble 2 to 3 minutes on medium-high until it has shrunk by half. Pour the onions and their sauce over the steaks.
steps.w: Browned onions plus the steak bits make a proper onion gravy with only water.
steps.c: The liquid is brown and coats the onions, with no pool of water left.
steps.m: Stopping too early so the gravy stays thin and pale.

title: Salmon with cauliflower mash
desc: Salmon on a smooth cauliflower mash, no potato.
trouble: Steam off the water in the hot pot before blending.

steps.t: Simmer the cauliflower for 10 minutes, drain and leave in the hot pot for 1 minute. Blend with the butter, cream and nutmeg.
steps.w: Dry cauliflower gives a thick mash.
steps.m: Blending wet makes soup.
steps.img: smooth cauliflower mash in a pot

steps.t: Pat the salmon dry, salt it and fry 4 minutes skin side and 2 on the other. Finish with lemon and parsley.
steps.w: Dry fish browns.
steps.m: Moving it too early tears the skin.
steps.img: salmon on cauliflower mash

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the salmon out and pour 3 tbsp water into the pan on medium heat, scraping the bottom with a wooden spoon. Add 2 tbsp of the cream and a squeeze of lemon and let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes until it coats the spoon. Season and spoon the sauce over the salmon.
steps.w: Salmon leaves tasty bits in the pan, and cream plus lemon makes a quick sauce that ties fish and mash together.
steps.c: It is pale, smooth and coats the back of the spoon.
steps.m: Boiling it hard on high so it splits and looks oily.

title: Mustard-crusted chicken with carrots
desc: Chicken fillet under a mustard and parsley crust, finished in the air fryer or oven.

steps.t: Simmer the carrots in a little salted water until just tender, then drain.
steps.w: A short cook keeps the bite and the colour.
steps.c: A knife goes in with slight resistance.
steps.m: Overcooked veg goes watery.
steps.img: a bowl of cooked carrots

steps.t: Salt the chicken and spread it with mustard. Press on the breadcrumbs mixed with parsley and oil.
steps.w: Mustard holds the crumbs on.
steps.m: A thick layer burns.
steps.img: chicken with a mustard crumb crust

steps.t: Air-fry at 190 °C for 15–18 minutes, or use the oven at 200 °C for 20.
steps.w: Hot air crisps the crust.
steps.m: Overcooking dries it out.
steps.img: mustard-crusted chicken with carrots

steps.t: Make the sauce: put the chicken on the plates and pour the juice from the air-fryer drawer (or oven tray) into a small bowl. Whisk in 1 tsp of the mustard and 1 tbsp water with a fork until smooth, then season. Spoon the sauce over the carrots and next to the chicken.
steps.w: The juice under the chicken carries the mustard crust flavour, and a little more mustard makes it a sauce.
steps.c: It is pale yellow, smooth and a bit thick.
steps.m: Pouring it over the crust so the crumbs go soggy.

title: Chicken and vegetable skillet with broccoli, carrots and peppers
desc: One pan, one lot of washing up, no sauce.
reheat: Pan with a splash of water.
trouble: Hotter pan, or fry in two batches.

steps.t: Fry the chicken in the oil on high for 4 minutes and lift out.
steps.w: Hot pan, browned meat.
steps.m: Crowding the pan.
steps.img: chicken strips in a pan

steps.t: Add carrots for 3 minutes, then broccoli and pepper for 4 with a splash of water.
steps.w: Hardest veg goes in first.
steps.m: Too much water steams everything.
steps.img: broccoli, carrots and peppers frying

steps.t: Return the chicken, add garlic, paprika and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
steps.w: Garlic burns if added early.
steps.m: Oversalting: soy sauce is already salty.
steps.img: a pan of chicken with broccoli, carrots and peppers

title: Scrambled eggs with salmon
desc: Soft scrambled eggs with a flaked salmon bar. Counts as a fish meal.
trouble: Take off the heat while still wet.
Fold it in at the end.

steps.t: Fry the salmon in half the butter for 3 minutes a side, then flake it.
steps.w: Cooking it first keeps the eggs soft.
steps.m: Overcooking dries it.
steps.img: flaked salmon in a pan

steps.t: Beat the eggs with salt. Melt the rest of the butter on low heat, add the eggs and stir for 3 minutes. Fold in salmon and dill.
steps.w: Low heat gives soft curds.
steps.m: High heat makes them dry.
steps.img: soft scrambled eggs with salmon and dill

title: Egg salad with carrot and pepper sticks
desc: Egg salad with mustard, no mayo.

steps.t: Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
steps.w: Cooling stops the yolk going grey.
steps.m: Lowering cold eggs into fast-boiling water cracks them.
steps.img: peeled boiled eggs

steps.t: Mix mustard, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper. Fold in the eggs, spring onion and parsley.
steps.w: The soft yolk thickens the dressing.
steps.m: Stirring hard mashes the egg.
steps.img: Egg salad with carrot and pepper sticks

title: Tuna salad with egg and tomato
desc: Tinned tuna, boiled egg and tomato with a mustard dressing. Counts as a fish meal.
trouble: Drain the tuna well, and salt the tomato late.

steps.t: Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool and quarter.
steps.w: Firm eggs hold their shape.
steps.m: Grey yolk means overcooked.
steps.img: quartered boiled eggs

steps.t: Make the dressing — the sauce for this salad: whisk the mustard, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper with a fork for 20 seconds until thick and cloudy. Toss with the tomato, onion and tuna, and top with egg and parsley.
steps.w: Whisked oil and acid turn into a thick, cloudy dressing that clings to the leaves instead of sliding off.
steps.m: Dressing early makes it watery.
steps.img: tuna salad with egg and tomato

title: Chicken salad with pepper and carrot
desc: Cold chicken fillet with crunchy veg and a mustard dressing.
trouble: Poach gently, and let it cool in the water.

steps.t: Poach the chicken in simmering salted water for 12 minutes. Leave it to cool a little and slice.
steps.w: Gentle poaching keeps it soft.
steps.m: A hard boil toughens it.
steps.img: sliced poached chicken

steps.t: Whisk mustard, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper. Toss with chicken, pepper, carrot, spring onion and parsley.
steps.w: Warm chicken takes up more dressing.
steps.m: Under-salting: taste it.
steps.img: chicken salad with peppers and grated carrot

title: Chicken skillet with peppers and cherry tomatoes
desc: A quick hot lunch from what is usually in the fridge.

steps.t: Fry the chicken in the oil on high heat for 4 minutes.
steps.w: Browning gives the flavour.
steps.m: Crowding the pan.
steps.img: chicken strips browning

steps.t: Add onion, pepper and garlic for 3 minutes, then tomatoes and paprika for 3 more. Season.
steps.w: Tomatoes go in last so they hold their shape.
steps.m: Burning the garlic.
steps.img: a pan of chicken with peppers and cherry tomatoes

steps.t: Press each tomato flat with the back of a fork so the juice runs into the pan. Add 4 tbsp water, scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 2 minutes on medium heat. Season and spoon the sauce over the chicken.
steps.w: The tomatoes only soften in 3 minutes; squashing them and adding water makes a paprika tomato sauce.
steps.c: It is red and thick enough to cling to the chicken.
steps.m: Stirring hard and breaking up the chicken instead of pressing the tomatoes.

title: Scrambled eggs with tomato and onion
desc: Hot, soft scrambled eggs with tomatoes and onion.

steps.m: Moving it around: it has to sit still to brown.
steps.img: paprika-rubbed chicken fillets browning in a pan

steps.t: While the chicken fries, boil the green beans for 5 minutes, then drain them.
steps.w: They cook in the time the chicken needs, so everything is ready together.
steps.c: Bright green, tender with a little bite.
steps.m: Boiling them until grey and soft.
steps.img: green beans draining in a colander

steps.t: Turn the heat to medium and push the chicken to one side. Add the rest of the oil and the sliced garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and the basil. Lay the mozzarella on the chicken, put the lid on and cook 5 minutes.
steps.w: Thin garlic slices soften and melt into the sauce. Tomato paste fried in oil gives the depth that fresh tomatoes alone do not have.
steps.c: Cheese melted, tomatoes collapsing, garlic soft and pale gold.
steps.m: Whole garlic cloves: in a pan they stay hard and cannot be mashed.
steps.img: chicken with melted mozzarella beside burst cherry tomatoes in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the chicken onto the plates. Press each tomato flat with a fork so the juice runs out, add 3 tbsp water and scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes until it clings to the spoon. Squeeze in the lemon, taste, and add the rest of the salt if it needs it. Turn the beans through the sauce, then plate them next to the chicken and spoon the rest over.
steps.w: Burst tomatoes, garlic, the browned rub and melted cheese in the pan fat become a sauce once you squash them and loosen with water. Lemon at the end makes it taste of something.
steps.c: Pink-red and thick enough to cling to the spoon and the beans.
steps.m: Serving without tasting: this is where the salt gets corrected.

title: Bolognese skillet with broccoli
desc: A fast mince and tomato sauce over broccoli, without the pasta. Counts as red meat.

steps.t: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes. Add onion, carrot and garlic for 4.
steps.w: Browning gives the sauce depth.
steps.m: Wet mince never browns.
steps.img: mince and vegetables in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: add the tomatoes and oregano, press any whole tomato pieces flat with the back of the spoon and simmer 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until a spoon dragged through leaves a trail. Cook the broccoli alongside and spoon the sauce over it.
steps.w: A short simmer brings it together.
steps.c: Thick sauce, the spoon leaves a trail.
steps.m: Too much liquid makes it soup.
steps.img: bolognese over broccoli

title: Fried eggs and tomato on flatbread
desc: Fried eggs and tomato on warm flatbread, without the ham.

steps.t: Make the tomato sauce: soften the tomatoes in half the butter for 2 minutes, press each one flat with a fork and stir 1 minute until thick and jammy, with no pool of juice. Warm the bread in a dry pan.
steps.w: Pressed tomatoes release their juice into the oil and turn into a sauce in a minute.
steps.m: Too much juice soaks the bread.
steps.img: cherry tomatoes softening

steps.t: Fry the eggs in the rest of the butter and lay them on the bread with the tomatoes and parsley.
steps.w: Medium heat keeps the white tender.
steps.m: High heat makes the edges rubbery.
steps.img: fried eggs on flatbread with tomatoes

title: Potato and chicken skillet with peppers
desc: A little fried potato with lots of chicken and peppers.
trouble: Leave them to brown before turning.
Add it back at the end.

steps.t: Boil the potatoes for 10 minutes and dice. Fry the chicken in half the oil for 5 minutes and lift out.
steps.w: Boiling first means less oil.
steps.m: Crowding the pan.
steps.img: chicken strips and diced potato

steps.t: Fry the potatoes, onion and pepper in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes. Add paprika and the chicken for 1 minute.
steps.w: Paprika goes in last.
steps.m: Burnt paprika tastes bitter.
steps.img: a pan of potatoes, peppers and chicken

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the potatoes and chicken onto the plates. Pour 4 tbsp water into the hot pan, scrape the paprika and potato crust off the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 1 minute on medium heat until slightly thick. Add salt and pepper and pour the sauce over.
steps.w: The paprika sticks to the pan and the water lifts it into a little sauce that stops the potatoes being dry.
steps.c: It is red-brown and slightly thick in under a minute.
steps.m: Using too much water so the crispy potatoes go soggy.

title: BBQ chicken wrap, no sugar
desc: Smoky chicken in flatbread with a sugar-free tomato BBQ sauce.

steps.t: Fry the chicken and onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Make the sauce in the pan: add the tomato paste, vinegar, smoked paprika and 3 tbsp water, scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon and let it bubble 1 minute until it turns sticky and coats every piece.
steps.w: Frying the paste gives a BBQ depth without sugar.
steps.c: Sticky, dark red, no liquid pooling.
steps.m: Too much water stops it sticking.
steps.img: smoky chicken strips in a pan

steps.t: Warm the bread in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side, fill and roll.
steps.w: Warm bread rolls without tearing.
steps.m: Overfilling splits it.
steps.img: a BBQ chicken wrap with lettuce

title: Chicken quesadilla with peppers
desc: Chicken and melted cheese between thin flatbreads, crisp from the pan.

steps.t: Fry the chicken and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes with the paprika and salt.
steps.w: A dry filling keeps the bread crisp.
steps.m: Wet filling makes it soggy.
steps.img: chicken and peppers in a pan

steps.t: Put filling and cheese on one half of each bread, fold, and fry 2 minutes a side.
steps.w: Medium heat melts the cheese before the bread burns.
steps.m: High heat burns it.
steps.img: a crisp chicken quesadilla cut in wedges

title: Carrot and potato mash with fried eggs
desc: Mashed carrot with a little potato, and fried eggs on top.
trouble: Steam off the water in the hot pot.

steps.t: Simmer carrots and potato for 13 minutes, drain, and mash with half the butter and the nutmeg.
steps.w: Dry veg mashes thick.
steps.m: Blending makes it gluey.
steps.img: mashed carrots in a pot

steps.t: Fry the eggs in the rest of the butter and serve on the mash.
steps.w: Medium heat keeps the white tender.
steps.m: Hard yolks.
steps.img: fried eggs on orange carrot mash

title: Cauliflower patties with feta and tomato
desc: Cauliflower patties with egg and feta. Keep it to the odd lunch, as cauliflower is limited.
trouble: Squeeze the cauliflower dry and chill.

steps.t: Simmer the cauliflower for 5 minutes, drain well and chop finely.
steps.w: Dry cauliflower holds together.
steps.m: Wet mix falls apart.
steps.img: finely chopped cauliflower

steps.t: Mix with eggs, feta, crumbs and parsley. Shape 6 patties and fry in the oil, 4 minutes a side.
steps.w: Feta seasons them.
steps.m: Turning too soon breaks them.
steps.img: golden cauliflower patties with tomatoes

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the patties out and put the halved cherry tomatoes into the same pan on medium heat for 3 minutes. Press each tomato flat with a fork, add 3 tbsp water, salt and pepper, and let it bubble 2 minutes while you scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon. Spoon the sauce next to the patties.
steps.w: The tomatoes are on the shopping list but never used, and squashed in the pan fat they make a quick fresh sauce.
steps.c: The tomatoes have collapsed into a loose, glossy red sauce with some skins.
steps.m: Not pressing the tomatoes, so you get whole hot tomatoes instead of a sauce.

title: Mince pizza on flatbread with onion
desc: Spiced mince and cheese on thin flatbread from the air fryer. Counts as red meat.

steps.t: Brown the mince and onion in the oil for 6 minutes and season. Make the sauce in the pan: stir in the tomato paste, oregano and 2 tbsp water and scrape the bottom for 1 minute until it is thick and sticky and coats the mince.
steps.w: Dry mince keeps the base crisp.
steps.c: Dark and sticky, no liquid left.
steps.m: Wet mince soaks the bread.
steps.img: dark mince in a pan

steps.t: Spread on the bread, top with mozzarella and air-fry at 180 °C for 5 minutes.
steps.w: Thin bread crisps fast.
steps.m: Too long burns the bread.
steps.img: flatbread pizza with mince and cheese

title: Feta scrambled eggs with peppers
desc: Scrambled eggs with peppers and your feta.
trouble: No extra salt: feta is salty.
goes: The tomato-pepper sauce is in the pan.

steps.t: Soften the pepper in the butter for 4 minutes until the edges brown.
steps.w: Soft pepper mixes in well.
steps.c: Soft, sweet, a few brown edges.
steps.m: Browning the butter.
steps.img: diced peppers softening

steps.t: Make the sauce: put the halved cherry tomatoes in cut side down and leave them 2 minutes. Press each tomato flat with a fork until the juice runs. Add the paprika, a pinch of salt and 2 tbsp water, scrape the brown bits off the pan with the fork and let it bubble 2 minutes.
steps.w: The pressed tomatoes, butter and pepper juices turn into a quick sauce, so the eggs are not dry.
steps.c: The sauce coats the back of a spoon and no longer looks watery.
steps.m: Stirring the tomatoes before they brown — they stay raw and watery.
steps.img: halved cherry tomatoes pressed flat with a fork in a frying pan with soft red pepper strips, glossy red pan sauce coating a spoon, home kitchen, top view

steps.t: Push the sauce to one side. Pour the beaten eggs into the free half on low heat and stir gently for 3 minutes. Fold in the feta, the sauce and the parsley.
steps.w: The eggs cook gently next to the sauce and pick it up when you fold.
steps.c: Soft and glossy, streaked with red sauce.
steps.m: High heat makes the eggs dry.
steps.img: scrambled eggs with feta and peppers

title: Pesto chicken with tomatoes and broccoli
desc: Chicken with a quick home pesto, so no sugar from a jar.

steps.t: Blend the basil, parmesan, walnuts, garlic, olive oil and a pinch of salt with a spoon of water.
steps.w: Walnuts cost less than pine nuts and work well.
steps.m: Long blending turns it bitter.
steps.img: green pesto in a blender

steps.t: Simmer the broccoli for 3 minutes and keep 2 tbsp of the water. Fry the chicken in the sunflower oil for 6 minutes, add the tomatoes for 2 and press each one flat with a fork. Make the sauce: take the pan off the heat, add the pesto and the broccoli water and stir for 20 seconds until glossy and it coats the chicken.
steps.w: Pesto loses its colour on high heat.
steps.m: Cooking the pesto dulls it.
steps.img: chicken with pesto, tomatoes and broccoli

left: Does not keep; the eggs go rubbery.
title: Egg and tomato wrap with lemon yogurt sauce
desc: Soft scrambled eggs with cherry tomatoes and onion in a thin flatbread, lemon and dill yogurt sauce on top.
trouble: Heat too high or left on too long. Take the pan off while they still look wet.
Too much lemon. Stir in one more spoon of yogurt.
ing: thin, wholemeal if they have it

steps.t: Make the sauce first: put the yogurt in a cup, squeeze in 2 teaspoons of lemon juice, add the dill and a pinch of salt and pepper. Stir with a fork for 20 seconds until it is smooth and drops slowly off the fork. Taste it; if it tastes flat, add a few more drops of lemon.
steps.w: Cold sauce made first, so the eggs do not wait.
steps.c: Smooth and white, thick enough to drop slowly off the fork.
steps.m: Pouring in the lemon all at once makes it runny.
steps.img: a cup of white yogurt sauce with dill and a fork, half a lemon beside it

steps.t: Melt the butter in the pan on medium heat. Fry the onion and the halved tomatoes for 2 minutes.
steps.w: Soft onion and warm tomatoes give the eggs their taste.
steps.c: Onion glassy, tomato skins starting to wrinkle.
steps.m: High heat browns the butter before the onion is soft.
steps.img: halved cherry tomatoes and chopped onion frying in butter in a pan

steps.t: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pour them over the tomatoes. Turn the heat down and push the eggs slowly across the pan for about 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat while they still look slightly wet.
steps.w: Eggs keep cooking in the hot pan after you take it off.
steps.c: Soft, shiny curds, no liquid egg running in the pan.
steps.m: Waiting until they look done in the pan makes them dry on the plate.
steps.img: soft scrambled eggs with cherry tomatoes in a pan

steps.t: Warm each flatbread for 20 seconds a side in a dry pan. Spread half of the sauce on the bread, lay the eggs down the middle, spoon the rest of the sauce over the eggs and roll it up.
steps.w: Warm bread rolls without tearing.
steps.c: Tight roll, sauce on the bread and on the eggs.
steps.m: Overfilling splits it.
steps.img: an egg and tomato wrap cut in half with white yogurt sauce

title: Sour garlic chicken in a tangy onion glaze (no honey)
desc: Browned chicken thighs in a sharp, dark glaze of onions, garlic, cider vinegar, soy and mustard. A classic sour onion sauce, here on chicken, and the sticky honey-garlic look without any honey.
reheat: Pan with a splash of water, lid on for 3 minutes.
left: Cold in a wrap with lettuce, or chopped into tomorrow's eggs.
trouble: Let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes longer: vinegar mellows as it reduces. A knob of butter rounds it off.
Add another tablespoon of vinegar at the end and let it bubble only 30 seconds, so it keeps its bite.
Soy sauce is salty: no extra salt in the sauce until you have tasted it at the end.
Lift the chicken out and let the sauce bubble on its own until it coats the spoon, then turn the chicken back through it.
It went brown: next time add it only 30 seconds before the tomato paste.
goes: Green beans or broccoli from the healthy sides; the glaze is good on both.

steps.t: Mix the salt, pepper and paprika and rub it over the chicken thighs on both sides.
steps.w: The seasoning on the meat browns into the crust that later colours the sauce.
steps.m: Seasoning only the sauce.
steps.img: raw boneless chicken thighs rubbed with paprika on a wooden board

steps.t: Heat the oil in the pan on medium-high. Lay the thighs in, smooth side down, and fry 5 minutes a side without moving them. Lift them onto a plate.
steps.w: A still thigh browns; the brown bits left in the pan are the base of the sauce.
steps.c: Deep golden on both sides, brown bits stuck to the pan.
steps.m: Moving them: they steam instead of browning.
steps.img: chicken thighs browning in a frying pan

steps.t: Turn the heat to medium. Fry the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes until soft and golden. Add the sliced garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomato paste for 30 seconds, stirring.
steps.w: Soft onions are the body of a sour onion sauce; frying the paste takes away its raw taste.
steps.c: Onions soft and golden, garlic pale gold, paste darkened to brick red.
steps.m: Adding the garlic with the onions: it burns before they are soft.
steps.img: sliced onions and garlic turning golden in a frying pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour in the cider vinegar, stand back from the steam, and scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon until no brown bits stick. Stir in the soy sauce, mustard and water, add the bay leaf, put the chicken back with its juices and let it bubble without a lid for 6 to 8 minutes, turning the thighs twice, until the sauce has reduced to a dark glaze that clings to the spoon. Taste: another spoon of vinegar if you want it sharper.
steps.w: Vinegar lifts the brown bits off the pan; reducing turns vinegar, soy and onion into a thick, sour glaze without honey or flour.
steps.c: Dark, shiny and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon; the thighs are glazed all over.
steps.m: Stopping while the sauce is still thin and watery.
steps.img: chicken thighs in a dark shiny vinegar glaze bubbling in a pan

steps.t: Take out the bay leaf. Plate the thighs, spoon the glaze and onions over and scatter the spring onion and chilli flakes.
steps.w: Fresh spring onion cuts through the rich glaze.
steps.m: Leaving the glaze in the pan.
steps.img: plated glazed chicken thighs with spring onion and chilli flakes

title: Stuffed chicken with mozzarella, tomato and basil in a creamy tomato sauce
desc: Chicken breasts filled with mozzarella, tomato and basil, browned, then finished in a cream and cherry-tomato pan sauce. The caprese chicken, seasoned from the inside.
reheat: Covered in a pan with a spoon of water, low heat, 5 minutes.
left: Sliced cold next day, or reheated with the sauce.
trouble: Close the pocket with 2 toothpicks and fry the open side last; a little cheese escaping into the sauce is fine.
The breast was too thick: next time flatten the thick end first, and keep the lid on for the last 5 minutes.
Let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes longer without the lid.
Salt the sauce at the end, a pinch at a time, then taste again.
goes: Green beans or broccoli from the healthy sides.

steps.t: Cut a deep pocket into the side of each chicken breast without cutting through. Rub the outside with the salt, pepper, paprika and oregano. Fill each pocket with basil leaves, tomato slices and mozzarella, and close it with 2 toothpicks.
steps.w: The filling seasons the meat from inside and keeps it juicy.
steps.c: Pockets full, closed, outside evenly red-brown.
steps.m: Cutting through the other side, so the filling falls out.
steps.img: chicken breasts stuffed with mozzarella, tomato and basil on a board

steps.t: Fry the chicken in the oil on medium-high, 5 minutes a side. Then turn to medium, put the lid on and cook 5 minutes more.
steps.w: Browning gives the crust; the lid cooks the thick stuffed middle through and melts the cheese.
steps.c: Golden on both sides, cheese starting to ooze.
steps.m: High heat with the lid on: burnt outside, raw inside.
steps.img: stuffed chicken breasts browning in a pan

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the chicken onto a plate. Fry the sliced garlic in the pan for 30 seconds, stir in the tomato paste for 30 seconds, add the cherry tomatoes and press each one flat with a fork. Pour in the cream and water, scrape the bottom of the pan and let it bubble 3 minutes until it clings to the spoon. Stir in the parmesan, taste, salt it, then put the chicken back and spoon the sauce over.
steps.w: Tomato paste and burst tomatoes give colour and depth; cream and the brown bits from the chicken make it a proper sauce.
steps.c: Pink-orange, thick enough to coat the spoon.
steps.m: Serving the chicken before the sauce has thickened.
steps.img: stuffed chicken in a creamy tomato sauce in a pan
